q: An approval names one device, but later evidence identifies a different device. What should the workflow do?
options: Return for a new scoped decision
Apply the original decision because the case number did not change
Choose both devices to preserve the responder's original intent
Use the original approval if the display name resembles the new one
explanation: The original decision binds the proposed effect to its explicit target.

q: Which two states should the gate record separately?
options: Time the case opened and the same time expressed in UTC
Workflow app name and displayed page name for that app
Incident type and a duplicate label from the same form
Authorised decision and verified operational effect
explanation: Authority to act and evidence of the effect answer different questions.

q: The approver replies before expiry but execution happens afterward under current-authority rules. What should happen?
options: Apply it because approval was seen at some point before expiry
Extend the approval automatically to cover the current target state
Obtain renewed authority before any execution
Close the case and assume no protective action is now justified
explanation: The action needs a valid decision at the point specified by policy.

q: What makes a protective request sufficiently scoped?
options: A verbal instruction to change anything that looks related
A specific target, effect, evidence and expiry
An urgent alert title and the owner's informal department label
A list of available actions without identifying the one intended
explanation: Clear scope lets the approver see exactly what permission means.

q: A pending decision receives no reply within the review window. What is a safe result?
options: Record expiry and route the unresolved risk
Proceed automatically because there was no objection
Treat the lack of reply as proof the risk was eliminated
Use the permit issued for an earlier case action instead
explanation: Silence is not authority and can require a separate escalation.

q: Which actor verifies the effect of the approved change?
options: The alert source without access to the target service
An unrelated person who only saw the original notification
The report template that displays the decision badge
The authorised owner using the relevant target evidence
explanation: Effect verification needs evidence of the resulting state.

q: An approved request expands from two mail items to twenty after a search rerun. What needs review?
options: Only the room where the earlier approval was entered
A revised display label that keeps the same original authority
A fresh decision covering the expanded match set
A check that all twenty share a similar filename or subject
explanation: Approval cannot be reused for a materially broader effect.

q: What helps verify an approver's authority in the exercise design?
options: An email footer containing the words incident lead
A decision recorded through an approved authenticated mechanism
A forwarded image of a response from an unknown source
A workflow comment saying an operator can act in emergencies
explanation: The record should establish the person and their relevant scope.

q: The user who requests a change is ineligible to approve it. What should the gate enforce?
options: The separation required by the approval policy
Permission because request submission demonstrates good intent
Automatic authority after the request has been open for some time
A new priority value that allows the same user to decide
explanation: Approval role and eligibility must be checked separately from authorship.

q: Why include a verification method in the request?
options: It lets the workflow ignore the target once the action is accepted
It makes the approval time equal to the start time of the effect
It removes the need for response records after a successful decision
It defines how the expected effect can be confirmed
explanation: The verification plan links approval intent to observable outcome.

q: The downstream owner confirms only half the requested scope changed. What should the record say?
options: Mark the whole request complete because part of it reached the service
Cancel the verified effect from the audit so status remains uniform
Verify the affected part and keep the remainder unresolved
Replace the original scope with the completed subset after the fact
explanation: Partially applied effects need distinct evidence and remaining ownership.

q: What should a denial record contain?
options: The credentials of the actor who might perform the action later
A reason and a route for unresolved risk where appropriate
The technical result that would have happened if the action ran
A default grant to apply the same outcome on another target
explanation: A denial can guide review without authorising the proposed step.

q: An emergency occurs outside normal approval hours. What determines any alternate route?
options: The organisation's documented emergency authority
The largest impact estimate submitted by the workflow author
The presence of several failed validation messages in the queue
Any individual analyst's preference about speed versus documentation
explanation: An emergency route still needs clear authority and a record of the scoped decision.

q: Which detail should an oncoming approver see in the pending queue?
options: Every sensitive case attachment in the general queue summary
Only a permanent link to the initial notification
The final response result before anyone has made the decision
Current request state, action, owner and expiry
explanation: A pending view should show actionable state and retain access boundaries.

q: How should missing or malformed approval data be handled?
options: Select approved as the most helpful default value
Operate on the most recent target while waiting for clarification
Stop the action and record review needed
Skip all future approval checks when the data error repeats
explanation: Technical uncertainty cannot substitute for an authorised decision.

q: What should a low-impact automated intake usually do when it only prepares a request?
options: Apply every requested change before the draft reaches the approver
Record a draft for authorised review if policy permits
Allow the alert to select its own downstream control credentials
Erase the receipt when the case remains undecided
explanation: Preparation can be permitted without allowing consequential effects.

q: The same approved request is delivered twice. How is a duplicate effect prevented?
options: Recheck the stable effect reference before changing state
Treat every new delivery timestamp as a distinct approval
Assume the first attempt did not reach the service
Request two independent protective changes so both receipts finish
explanation: Multiple deliveries may represent the same authorised operation.

q: What belongs with the rationale for an approval?
options: Only the case label because evidence is optional for a decision
The identities of unrelated employees drawn from similar incidents
A statement that every action can be completely undone
The evidence, anticipated scope and operational impact
explanation: Reviewers need enough context to judge benefit, risk and scope.

q: A notification says approved, but the case's live request is now cancelled. Which state controls action?
options: The earlier text in the notification because it was received first
The dashboard's last successful result for a nearby case
The current authorised request state
The responder's assessment that action could be useful anyway
explanation: The notification is historical evidence; the live gate can invalidate permission.

q: What should a paper test use to represent the protected target?
options: A production endpoint that other teams are using
A fictional ID and a mocked control outcome
A real employee's active access session
A live connector with broad write privileges
explanation: Synthetic state gives sufficient evidence for training without production changes.

q: The first approved action depends on a step that remains unverified. What result is appropriate?
options: Keep execution pending until its prerequisite is established
Apply it immediately because every approved action ignores dependencies
Operate using the later action's approval instead of confirming the prerequisite
Treat a pending dependency as a standard decline of the visible request
explanation: Authority does not remove operational or evidentiary preconditions.

q: Why link a decision to a request revision?
options: It allows later requests to inherit unrelated approval
It records the name of the interface used to style the request
It removes the need to preserve scope and evidence
It identifies the exact proposal the person reviewed
explanation: Revision binding helps detect changes before the existing approval is used.

q: A denial arrived under the wrong case identifier. What can be concluded?
options: The current request is denied because an unrelated record says denied
Convert the wrong-case decision into permission for the current operation
Reconcile the reference before applying it to this request
Close both cases because neither can be reliably evaluated
explanation: A decision only applies when its case and scoped request can be verified.

q: What gives approvers a practical alternative to broad exposure of artifacts?
options: A copy of every raw record in a broadly distributed approval message
A short scoped summary with a restricted evidence reference
A shared worksheet containing unrelated credentials and contexts
A full unredacted report sent before deciding whether it is needed
explanation: A restricted reference provides detail to eligible reviewers when needed.

q: Which lesson exercise tests consideration of updated scope?
options: Change the target after a mock approval and check for a safe stop
Rotate the colours of the approval progress badge in the example
Run the same calculation several times without changing any input
Move the existing approval message to a different display folder
explanation: The test verifies whether the gate detects an unapproved material change.
